notes.note: Dio explains why he records the date: after the battle Caesar (Octavian) for the first time held all power alone, presenting Actium as the turning point to sole rule.
notes.quotation: but Caesar now for the first time held all the power alone,

notes.note: Caesar (Octavian) commemorates the victory by dedicating captured ships to Apollo of Actium, enlarging his temple, and founding the Actia festival.
notes.quotation: In honour of the day he dedicated to Apollo of Actium from the total number of the captured vessels a trireme, a quadrireme, and the other ships in order up to one of ten banks of oars

notes.note: Dio reads the day of the battle as the start of Caesar's sole power, so the years of his reign are reckoned from it.
notes.quotation: and consequently the years of his reign are properly reckoned from that day.

notes.note: Dio reports Caesar's commemoration of the victory: founding Nicopolis on the site of his camp and building an Apollo shrine adorned with captured ship beaks.
notes.quotation: adorned it with the captured beaks, and erected on it, open to the sky, a shrine of Apollo.
